name: flour_prices
title: Tiao and Box's tools: flour prices in three cities
summary: The Wisconsin tools on the data Tiao and Tsay (1989) analysed: monthly flour price indices in Buffalo, Minneapolis and Kansas City, 1972-1980, from three univariate models built with art's identification. Box and Tiao's (1977) canonical analysis of the levels and Tiao and Box's (1981) stepwise M(l) say what the univariates' differences hide: the prices move together, and the joint model may not need every difference.
plan: N1 run_gate — the three univariate models, certified
N1b canonical_analysis — Box and Tiao (1977) on the levels: one common trend, and a contrast between markets
N2 identify_cross — innovations correlated at 0.96: the same shocks
N2 identify_matrices — Tiao and Box's stepwise M(l) beside Jenkins and Alavi's S_k, on the differences
N3 estimate — the VAR(1) M(l) asks for
N5 evaluate — the yardstick: does it forecast better than the univariates?
